builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: When the Consumer Is an Agent: Execution-Grounded Service-Level Agreements
summary: The technique replaces the LLM agent's self-reported task completion with an independent control plane that observes a deadline-bound service-state predicate, admits or rejects completion, and directs recovery. It costs an additional control-plane component, state-predicate instrumentation per service, and deadline monitoring that can delay or reject legitimately completed work when observation lags. It can fail when state predicates are mis-specified, when observability of the target service is itself delayed or incomplete, or when healthy tasks are terminated as unverified due to monitoring faults rather than task faults.
rationale: Replacing agent self-assessment with deadline-bound verification of service state is implementable on constrained infrastructure, but the paper evaluates only placement and deletion in one data service, so the reader should validate it on their own workflows before production adoption.
technique: Execution-grounded completion contracts via independent control plane

claims.statement: The technique replaces the LLM agent's self-reported task completion with an independent control plane that observes a deadline-bound service-state predicate, admits or rejects completion, and directs recovery. It costs an additional control-plane component, state-predicate instrumentation per service, and deadline monitoring that can delay or reject legitimately completed work when observation lags. It can fail when state predicates are mis-specified, when observability of the target service is itself delayed or incomplete, or when healthy tasks are terminated as unverified due to monitoring faults rather than task faults.

Under enforcement, all included healthy tasks completed, accepted completions remained consistent with later observations, and unresolved faulted tasks terminated as unverified; without enforcement, some deadline-missing tasks were accepted and some deadline-meeting tasks were rejected.
